title: The Witcher 3 updated system requirements are in, and you will need an RTX 5080 for path tracing with DLSS and frame generation
summary: And CD Projekt Red doesn't state what that upscaling mode means.
body: We all know that path tracing is a bit of a GPU hog, and if you plan on running it in the remaster of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt , you're going to need a beefy and relatively new rig for this graphical mode. However, to get the game up and running on the lowest settings at 30 fps, you won't need a very recent GPU. With The Witcher 3 Remastered going live today, CD Projekt Red has shared what you can expect to run with every major CPU and GPU brand, with Low graphics at 30 fps requiring a relatively meagre Nvidia GeForce GTX 1660 / AMD Radeon RX 550 XT / Intel Arc A580 , plus an Intel Core i5 8400 or AMD Ryzen 5 2600. However, for path tracing, you will need an Intel Core i9 13900K or AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D , paired with an Nvidia GeForce RTX 5080 . To get the estimated 60 fps at 4K, you will have to not only run DLSS, but you will need to use frame generation. That does mean it should fare better at 1440p or 1080p. CD Projekt Red does not specify which level of upscaling (though it says it's on Auto, whatever that means) or what level of frame generation is present for this setting. As we saw in our investigation of Pragmata's path tracing earlier this year, we are expecting The Witche…

title: How to get unlocked Multi Frame Gen working on an RTX 40-series graphics card
summary: Who needs an RTX 5090, right?
body: Just in case you've been napping under a cool mossy rock since about January 2025, Multi Frame Generation (or MFG) is a frame rate boosting/game smoothing feature that leverages AI to create as many as five frames for every actually rendered frame. Nvidia introduced the original 2x Frame Generation feature with the RTX 40-series graphics cards in 2022. Sadly Nvidia restricted the more recent Multi Frame Generation version of the tech to RTX 50-series cards alone . Mmm, buttery; boo, proprietary. But before you rush out to search in vain for an RTX 5090 at MSRP , it is possible to get most of the extra smoothness of MFG working on older Nvidia graphics cards—if you don't mind a little bit of software tinkering. Before I tell you how, there's a few things to note. For one thing, Nvidia restricted higher rates of MFG to the RTX 50-series cards for a reason. At the risk of oversimplifying, the RTX 50-series' silicon is specifically designed to manage the extra frames in ways the older architecture is not. There's a dedicated AI Management Processor (AMP) which works alongside Flip Metering to get frames—rendered and generated—delivered to the display in as smooth a way as possible. Th…

title: How to unlock transmog in The Witcher 3 Remastered
summary: Level up Geralt's fashion game by changing his sword and armor skins.
body: Key deets ⚔️ You can transmog armor with Yoana at Crow's Perch after the Master Armorers quest. ⚔️ You can transmog swords with Hattori in Novigrad after the Of Swords and Dumplings quest. ⚔️ Any armor or sword Geralt picks up unlocks as a skin. ⚔️ It costs 100-200 coin every time you swap skins. One of the big changes in The Witcher 3 Remastered is that you can now transmog armor and swords, swapping their skins at will. You can't transmog at every blacksmith, only the two master smiths in the game, Yoana at Crow's Perch, and Éibhear Hattori in Novigrad, who will let you reskin armor and swords, respectively. First, though, you have to complete their quests: Master Armorers Speak to Fergus Graem, the dwarf armorer at Crow's Perch, and ask about mastercrafted armor. Then Yoana will ask you to travel to Undvik in Skellige to recover some blacksmith tools. Of Swords and Dumplings Speak to Éibhear Hattori at his shop in Novigrad, northwest of Glory Gate, to start his quest and unlock him as a blacksmith. Once you've unlocked Yoana and Hattori, simply choose the "reforge" tab on the top right when purchasing or crafting with them. You can find Yoana in Crow's Perch castle CD Projekt A…

title: How to get the Wolven armor in The Witcher 3

title: I can't stop comparing the dialogue from the original, messy FF7 localization and its vastly improved fan translation
summary: The Shinra Archaeology Cut of FF7 gives the game the treatment Square Enix's official PC release deserved.
body: "Final Fantasy 7 PC" is not an immediately intuitive combination of numbers and letters. Am I talking about the old trapezoid box version released in 1998? Or the "remaster" re-released in 2013? Or the first in the trilogy of remakes released nearly a decade later? Calling the 1998 version the "original" just makes things more confusing, since it isn't exactly the same as the PlayStation game released the year before. When Square Enix updated Final Fantasy 7 to modern platforms in 2013 it had the chance to create something like the definitive version of the game, but instead it took some shortcuts, "improving" a few things from the original—like some of the notoriously rushed translation's grammatical mistakes—but more or less leaving the rest untouched. It's a worst of both worlds combination, where funny lines like "this guy are sick" get corrected to "this guy is sick" but the script as a whole remains confusing and frequently misrepresented in English. Two years ago, fans released a monumental mod called the Shinra Archaeology Cut aimed at doing the script justice with a complete, top-to-bottom retranslation. It's one of a heap of FF7 mods available in the fan launcher 7th Hea…

title: Former Elder Scrolls writer Kurt Kuhlmann is '100% convinced' a load-bearing bit of series lore was inspired by a typo
summary: The Warp in the Draft.
body: Speaking on the FRVR Podcast last week, former Bethesda writer and designer Kurt Kuhlmann was asked about the concept of " Dragon Breaks "—time getting all weird on account of magic and stuff⁠—in Elder Scrolls lore. The biggest Dragon Break as far as Elder Scrolls fans are concerned: "The Warp in the West," the series' post-facto determination that every ending of The Elder Scrolls Chapter 2: Daggerfall happened at the same time. On account of magic and stuff, you see. I love this story: Simple serendipity, a workplace oopsie, accidentally setting in motion the continuity and story beats of a billion-dollar franchise. Kirkbride is memetically famous among Elder Scrolls fans as a boundary-pushing loremaster who added a lot of weird flavor to Morrowind, so his affinity for the timey-wimey, fucky-wucky potential of the Dragon Break absolutely scans. As far as I can tell, it doesn't seem like the series timeline Kuhlmann mentioned was ever publicly available⁠—this must have been an internal lore bible sort of thing. title: Double Fine's first game since being dumped by Xbox will be out in just 2 weeks
summary: I don't know what I expected, but Thank You Bus Driver sure isn't it. It does look like fun, though.
body: It's been less than three months since Xbox kicked Double Fine Productions to the curb as part of the great "streamlining" that Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella is so excited to see . And just two weeks from today, the studio will release the first game of its post-Xbox existence: It's not what I expected, but it is most definitely a Double Fine game. Thank You Bus Driver is a driving sim, but not of the sort you'd find in the Bus Simulator series. There are three—and only three—priorities: Get To Your Next Stop , no matter what it takes Keep the Schedule , because happy riders say thank you No Breaking the Rules , and if anyone gets out of line, you give 'em a smack Over on Bluesky, Double Fine described Thank You Bus Driver as "Crazy Taxi meets Papers, Please!" which sounds like exactly the sort of game the studio would make—this is, after all, the studio that gave us a multiplayer brawling game about pottery . Clock in, drive the bus, and get passengers to their stops...but SLAP anyone breaking the rules (or throw 'em out the back if they don't behave)! It's Crazy Taxi meets Papers, Please! title: World of Warcraft: Forever players find black market NPC who sells a 15-day movement speed buff and other rare items that nobody can afford yet
summary: Blizzard is also using it to get ahead of price inflation.
body: Even though World of Warcraft: Forever is only in beta right now, players are able to explore a good amount of Azeroth to see what secrets Blizzard has tucked away for the full release. Several secrets have been found, like a bunch of hidden books that reward powerful leveling items, but some of them have hints for what to expect when it launches in November. There are plenty of items that don't have a clear use yet that might become extremely valuable as time goes on. A new NPC was recently found in the new Riverglades zone who sells a bunch of expensive crafting items. Theoretically, you should be able to get these items by playing the game normally, but many WoW: Forever players suspect he exists to prevent the auction house prices from skyrocketing due to their rarity. Mister Graphed, the black market goblin merchant , sells items for 20+ gold—a hefty chunk of change in the Classic-era of WoW—that should prevent anyone from feeling obligated to buy them for more than that from other players. title: A 'fundamental' update for this 34-year-old survival game is coming in October
summary: Are you ready to make some socks?
body: Survival game UnReal World is getting an update this October: Here's why that's rad: The game launched in 1992 and it's still getting patches The 34-year-old game is considered the first open world survival game —it even has a Guinness World Record for it Its creator, Sami Maaranen, has no plans to stop updating it : "When I accomplish one feature, I always have two more waiting" The update will bring " fundamental new clothcrafting features " to UnReal World This isn't just some simple outfits being added: " the most complex garments [take] days and days to craft " That last bullet is important. Materials for garments are expensive: one of the screenshots in the patch notes shows a woman, Heta, bartering for nine feet of linen cloth with another characher. title: Steam's tidying game trend is about to get the haunted meat it's been missing
summary: Something is Wrong with the Library is bringing some much-needed texture to organizing sims.
body: What happened: I Am Your Beast and Clickolding developer Strange Scaffold has announced Something is Wrong with the Library , a tidying game set in "a library haunted by blood and meat." Players will both reshelve the library's scattered books with a real Dewey Decimal System implementation while facing the accursed energies emanating from the corpses its billionaire patron entombed in the walls . A "Modular Chaos System" ensures each playthrough has its own set of books to reorganize. There's at least one terrifying, inscrutable obelisk. Something is Wrong with the Library is set to launch before the end of 2026. It's nice to see some aura in the tidying space In recent months, Steam has been awash in organize-em-ups and haystack searchers —games capitalizing on the simple pleasure of arranging a chaotic melange into an orderly assemblage. But while I'd never think to deny the meditative appeal of putting a thing in a place, I'm not going to pretend that the emergent craze isn't undergoing the same gold rush of low-effort iteration that we saw during the rash of retail sims. title: I have broken GTA 5 by installing so many mods that the game only launches in windowed mode now
summary: Which I'm taking as a… win?
body: Los Santos Customs I'm modding GTA 5 every day in a quest to either transform it into a PC version of GTA 6 or break it entirely. Come back tomorrow to find out what new horrible thing I've done to Rockstar's baby, or check out what I got up to earlier . Can a game go on life support? Can it begin, in its dotage, to show signs of the ailment that everyone knows—but would never say—is the thing that will one day bring it down for good? Grand Theft Auto 5 can. Installing my latest mod, Dynamic Traffic Colours , has brought my installation of the game to the point that it's failing death rolls. It will only launch in windowed mode, now. Trying to fullscreen the game before it has loaded will leave you suspended in the void. Quite literally: you will reside in an eternal black screen from which escape is impossible, unless you hold CTRL+ALT+DEL. Anyway, once I was in and windowed, I encountered a mystery. title: A love letter to the Guitar Hero X-Plorer Controller
summary: Simply the best.
body: I peaked at 16 years old. I was part way through an expert run of 'Through the Fire and the Flames' by Dragonforce on Guitar Hero 3 at a friend's house for their birthday, and I remember thinking to myself, 'I don't think I'll ever top this'. As the song came to an end and I revelled in my passing grade, I got at least one nod of approval from the group before they slunk off to do what actually cool 16-year-olds do when presented with a free house and no adults around: smoke a big joint. I've given it my all, on that same 20-year-old X-Plorer, with one of my favourite songs from that time. Scroll down for my cool video. Not me, though. I got high on sweet riffs, adeptly played out across five colourful buttons, slapped in near-perfect rhythm alongside a singular strum bar. Learn a real guitar? No, thanks. I'd rather sink 100s of hours into a rough approximation of the real thing—a karaoke version wrought of thin plastic from scaled-down body to hollow head unit. Plugged not into an amp, but an Xbox 360, with a whammy bar modulating not the strings, but the signal. body: (Image credit: CD Projekt) Key deets 🐺 The Witcher 3 Remastered releases on September 29. 🐺 There is no preload since it's an update. 🐺 The update size is about 45GB. The Witcher 3 Remastered releases this week, bringing updated visuals, a tonne of quality of life tweaks, and even some new features like armor transmog, to the 10-year-old RPG. The update arrives on September 29 everywhere, with a rolling release time throughout the day that's the same for both PC and console. Here's exactly when you can play: West Coast US : 3 am PDT East Coast US : 6 am EDT UK : 11 am BST Europe : 12 pm CEST Australia : 8 pm AEST New Zealand : 11 pm NZDT You can see the other times in the image above. title: Steam Week in Review: Great, haystack slop is a thing now
summary: All the interesting Steam facts for the week ending September 27.
body: Clones have been a fixture in the games industry forever. For every Mario Bros there's a Giana Sisters, for every Stardew Valley there's a Fields of Mistria, and for every Needle In A Haystack Simulator there's a A Needle In a Haystack, or Needle in a Haystack, or Needle In A Haystack, or Needle In A Haystack - A Time For Goats, or Story of The Needle In a Haystack. The total slopification of Steam continues apace and the recent spray of haystack games is the purest manifestation of this phenomenon. The first—as far as I can tell—was Needle In A Haystack Simulator, which is scheduled for release in Q4 2026. According to developers Studio Bitdot, a playtest in August attracted around 23,000 players , which is an astonishing figure for a game about finding a needle in a haystack. I'm not surprised that Needle In A Haystack Simulator is popular, mind you. Games about meaningless and repetitive labour are all the rage . Needle In A Haystack Simulator hybridises sorting and incremental games: the player must manually sift through hay to find the needle, but sifting will also unearth items that can be sold for profit, all the better to invest in more efficient hay sorting technology. title: Industry insiders and Tokyo gossip suggest Kojima is getting less money from Xbox than original PlayStation budget for Physint
summary: Whatever this game costs, people seem to agree it's in the nine figures.
body: The facts: Hideo Kojima's return to stealth-action, Physint, is no longer a PlayStation joint, and Microsoft picked up the ball . It still has big Hollywood talent, with Bill Skarsgård in the lead role . That's literally it. What people are saying: Alright, so what does that mean? Both Corden and Schreier's sources suggest Kojima Productions is working on a tighter budget with Microsoft than it was with Sony It's unclear how much had already been spent on Physint, and how much of the work on it is transferable—Kojima Productions presumably no longer has access to Sony's proprietary Decima Engine, for example. GamesRadar quoted a rumored budget for Death Stranding 2 "somewhere between $150-200 million." Insomniac's Spider-Man 2, with a leaked budget of $300 million , is widely agreed to have been an expensive gamble for PlayStation. Scooping Kojima was a PR victory for Xbox amid its unpopular, studio-killing "Reset," but its continued financial woes would give them incentive for doing it on the cheap. Whether Sony pulling out was a surprise as Kojima says , or preceded by months of negotiations, as alleged by Bloomberg , Kojima would not have been negotiating from a place of streng…

title: After 12 years, Dark Souls 2 is finally playable in co-op without interruptions
summary: Community maestro Yui made similar mods for Elden Ring and the original Dark Souls.
body: I've always been content to admire the Dark Souls games from afar, rather than get particularly into them myself, and part of that is probably a crumb of leftover resentment from trying to wrangle the multiplayer features in those early games. Love it or hate it, it's esoteric at the best of times and not terribly consistent. If you've a mind to mod those annoyances out of Dark Souls 2, now's your chance. That's thanks to Yui, a soulslike modder who made similar mods for Elden Ring and Dark Souls . Her latest creation, Dark Souls 2: Seamless Co-op , just released into alpha last week and promises a straightforward co-op experience with up to five other players. "With this, it's theoretically possible to play the game from the tutorial up to the final boss completely in one co-op session," the release blog on Patreon notes. I'm sure one of you will be doing just that with a DDR mat or something. While you could try to do a full playthrough with a buddy in the original Dark Souls 2, it'd involve a lot of stopping, starting, summoning, and fog walls. With this mod, there are no fog walls, progression is synced up, and the session won't end when someone dies—instead, they respawn at t…

title: Latest Xbox layoffs reportedly devastated Age of Empires developer and canceled its next game
summary: Microsoft continues to slash and burn the legacies under its banner.
body: The latest stage of Xbox's delicately named " reset " arrived last Tuesday —but its impact on World's Edge Studio, the developer now behind the Age of Empires series, was only briefly mentioned in Xbox CCO Matt Booty's announcement. On sites like resetera and LinkedIn, former employees of the RTS developer have shared that it was hit especially hard. "What a morning," said former World's Edge creative director Adam Isgreen on resetera , posting under the verified account name Tempus Chaoti. "FYI World's Edge was not spared completely—just under half the studio was let go—myself included. Been fun, y'all!" This is in addition to the studio now answering to Activision alongside Sea of Thieves developer Rare. Andrew Martz, former senior software engineer at World's Edge, posted on LinkedIn adding that "as part of that reorg, our next project was canceled and a large chunk of our studio was laid off. I was part of that layoff." Isgreen also had more to say on LinkedIn , reflecting on his time working on the RTS series: "I didn't think I'd be working on RTS games again years after their first 'heyday,' but am I ever proud of what our studio team and partners were able to do with the se…

title: William Pugh, co-designer of The Stanley Parable, has over 1,600 hours in Dota 2: 'It's not a game made of love. It's a game fuelled by hate and a desire to conquer'
summary: The founder of Crows Crows Crows guides us through the games on his PC.
body: Disk Cleanup (Image credit: Future) Welcome to Disk Cleanup , our regular weekend feature delving into the PCs of PC gaming luminaries. Come back every weekend to read a new interview, digging into the important questions, like "How tidy is your desktop?" and "What game will you never uninstall?" William Pugh grew up on a diet of shareware Mac titles like 1993's Scruffy versus the Invaders from Mars , but his earliest PC gaming memory is engaging in annelid antics in Worms 4: Mayhem—his first encounter with online multiplayer: "I remember playing that for the first time with random matchmaking," he says. "I think it was a 1v1 or whatever, and you're face-to-face with a complete stranger … I remember that being a kind of door opening for me." That door would lead Pugh into the cartoonish arenas of Team Fortress 2 , which in turn introduced him to the Source engine mapping community. Eventually, this brought Pugh in contact with fellow modder Davey Wreden, with whom he would write and design The Stanley Parable —2013's gleeful poke at player agency, and a remake of Wreden's mod of the same name. Following The Stanley Parable's success, Pugh founded Crows Crows Crows, which specialis…

title: Lords of the End Times' greatest fantasy is letting us rewrite the most hated lore in Warhammer's history
summary: The end of The End Times.
body: Play This Right Now Welcome to Play This Right Now, the site version of our weekly newsletter in which we celebrate a new game, update, or DLC that we think is well worth checking out. You can subscribe to the newsletter at the link if you want to get our thoughts about a new videogame happening direct to your inbox every Thursday. If you told me 10 years back, when I started playing Total War: Warhammer as a brighter-eyed and bushier-tailed strategy gamer, that we'd eventually reach The End Times period, I wouldn't have believed you. But here we are: three games, 110 legendary lords and factions later, Immortal Empires has successfully sliced and diced the best bits of Warhammer Fantasy and chucked them in a big cooking pot of delicious fantasy goodness. It's both the biggest and best Total War campaign Creative Assembly has ever attempted and you can now play it for just $9 (£7.49) by purchasing any of the characters from the Lords of the End Times expansion. title: Minecraft is getting its first new dimension in 15 years, and it is riotously pink
summary: Prepare to enter the Sift.
body: Since its release in 2011, Minecraft has received countless new biomes, but its number of dimensions has remained consistent over the last fifteen years. But that's all about to change. As of next year, a fourth dimension will soon join the Overworld, the Nether, and the End. It's called the Sift, it is riotously pink, and features bunny-like creatures that walk rather than hop. The Sift was revealed at the end of Saturday's Minecraft Live. In a brief clip showing the perambulating rabbit strolling through tufts of pink grass beneath a turquoise sky. Mojang didn't reveal much else about the Sift, but being a whole new dimension, players can naturally expect to encounter new mobs, blocks, biomes and so forth. While the Sift is coming to both Bedrock and Java versions of Minecraft in 2027, players will be able to explore a variant of the dimension before that. This is because the Sift will also appear in Minecraft Dungeons 2 when it releases next week, and we do know a little more about what form the realm will take in Mojang's ARPG sequel.
